newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Police hold hopes for Australia landslide survivors.
newsitem.headline: Police hold hopes for Australia landslide survivors.

text.p: Australian police on Thursday said they held hopes of finding survivors from a landslide that destroyed two ski lodges in Australia's Snowy Mountains, which is believed to have buried up to 20 people.
"We do hold some hopes that there may be some survivors," said police commander Bruce Johnston, adding the rescue operation may take up to two days.

Police and ski resort officials said that up to 20 people are believed to have been buried in the two lodges, including a number of Americans, when the landslide occured just before midnight on Wednesday.

Eyewitnesses reported hearing voices from the rubble shortly after the landslide, but police said there had been no sign of life in the past 12 hours. "Those cries stopped fairly early in the piece," said Johnston.
Police said a full rescue operation had been delayed because of fears of further landslides at the Thredbo Alpine Village, about 300 km (190 miles) southwest of Sydney.

"In fact, the advice we have is that there probably will be another small earth slip today. We're endeavouring to minimise the danger to the people working on this rescue operation," said police chief superintendent Charlie Sanderson.
